headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP can leak or be hijacked, while Taipy’s local/no-egress profile reduces but does not eliminate pairwise workflow risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP over stdio/SSE and browsers, so attacker-controlled content can reach its tool-use path. Taipy has no documented I/O surfaces, so the direct bridge is undocumented; uncertainty pushes this above low. The pair lacks a proven shared channel, but LightAgent’s runtime hooks and MCP make instruction hijack plausible if Taipy feeds it content.
conditions: IF Taipy is wired to pass rendered text or files into LightAgent via MCP or stdin/stdout, prompt injection becomes active.
IF LightAgent parses browser or API content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer tool calls.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Taipy outputs into LightAgent.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.
Require a human approval step before LightAgent tool calls.
Strip instructions from any Taipy-generated text before forwarding.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between data and instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and has broad network egress plus secret handling, so it can exfiltrate sensitive data if it receives it. Taipy is documented as network-egress none, but the pair still creates a leakage path from shared data into LightAgent’s outbound channels. The shared workspace is not documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Taipy forwards user data, workflow state, or files into LightAgent, that data can leave via LightAgent network egress.
IF LightAgent is given API keys or memory-backed context, those secrets may be transmitted to third-party APIs.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets into LightAgent context.
Restrict LightAgent egress to an allowlist.
Keep Taipy and LightAgent on separate workspaces.
Rotate any API keys used by LightAgent.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before cross-agent handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and broad network/subprocess/browser actions, while Taipy is a data-engineering framework with no documented write surfaces or concurrency model. There is no evidence of shared mutable resources or overlapping write scopes, so a direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because Taipy’s write behavior is undocumented, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same filesystem or database path, write conflicts can occur.
IF Taipy is extended with mutable external resources, concurrent updates may race with LightAgent actions.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same dataset.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool calls and workflow state, and Taipy is a scheduler/data-engineering system that may consume upstream outputs. If Taipy treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream jobs. The pairwise handoff is not directly documented, so this is inferred, but the default risk is still meaningful because LightAgent can emit unverified outputs.
conditions: IF Taipy schedules jobs using LightAgent-produced text or structured outputs without validation, errors propagate downstream.
IF LightAgent hallucinates facts that Taipy converts into actions, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Validate LightAgent outputs against schemas.
Insert a review step before Taipy executes actions.
Log and diff all upstream outputs.
Limit Taipy to read-only consumption of LightAgent results.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles secrets and user conversations, while Taipy’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency/compliance constraints. No concrete residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because its profile lacks compliance metadata.
conditions: IF LightAgent processes regulated data without a matching retention or residency policy, compliance exposure increases.
IF Taipy is used to store or export the same regulated data class, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through LightAgent.
Document retention for both systems.
Separate regulated and unregulated workflows.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and audit logs.
